linkedin.post:
1.5 million passengers were due to fly from US airports on Friday evening when every departure was halted for more than four hours.

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blames ageing routers and switches that overloaded with data. Homeland Security says there is no sign of a cyber attack so far, and is checking whether a new AI routing tool played a part.

Flights from Sydney to the US were briefly held, and some Australians were stranded.

Should air traffic control be rebuilt fast, or is rushing in new AI the bigger risk? Tell us what you think below.

#AusSight #AI #Aviation

warnings: Cause not officially confirmed: 'old routers' is US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's account and is attributed to him in the video and posts.
Duration: ABC News (US) gives 3:54pm-8:15pm ET (about 4h21m); ABC News Australia reports 'more than five hours'. Video and posts say 'more than four hours'.
Single-source figures: US$12.5B approved by Congress and US$30.1B requested (Al Jazeera, 13 Nov 2026).
Cancellation totals conflict between reports (about 4,700 to almost 10,000), so none are used.
Whether the new AI tool (SMART) contributed is under review; officials have not established a link and its developer denies one.
